searchText: <@552133098075193354> (or anyone else who knows) is there a high level "specification" (the more human readable the better) for withdraws that is relatively up to date with current thinking? I know there is the EL EIP, and the CL PR. I was hoping for something more like an architecture overview that links to those documents and is more consumable by a broader audience. There is a metaspec, https://notes.ethereum.org/@ralexstokes/validator-withdrawals-meta-spec Not sure how representative it is for broader audience and not sure whether it is up to date or not, cc <@539495253418180618> There were some notes written by Danny a long ago that were linked in the CL specs. They were nicely written for everyone I think. Probably they are not up to date in technical details like the queue, but that's not important from an end-user perspective https://twitter.com/polarpunklabs/status/1597207420027011072 Academic article that discusses Ethereum + a summary of development, dev culture, etc. Namechecks a few of you guys, so hopefully of some meta-intrigue! 'This paper inquires into the dynamic imaginaries of the Ethereum project. We present Ethereum as animated by three such imaginaries: the world computer (technical), productive money (economic) and public goods (political). We examine how these imaginaries are materialized, carried forward and evolve through the Ethereum ecosystem, focusing on how Ethereum’s prefigurative logic underpins this dynamism. In our analysis, we pay particular attention to how the imaginaries overlap and often generate contradictions that nonetheless do not seem to undermine the cohesion of the project. We introduce the concept of ‘prefigurative imaginaries’ to describe how prefiguration works to create multiple, mutually entangled but distinct imaginaries.' you'll have a better chance of anyone reading it if you post it on the arxiv. Most people in technical research institutions won't have access to an obscure journal "Social Epistemology " The journal is called Economy and Society and is a top ranked business journal. I have the following link https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/02691728.2022.2086086 weird, try again from here: https://twitter.com/polarpunklabs/status/1597207420027011072 ahhh I was lead to a similarly named article, let me check that one https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/03085147.2022.2131280?scroll=top&needAccess=true still no access here I would not send a link to "Social Epistemology " in here ha. Under the tweet I ask anyone interested to DM me for a copy. in a few days it will get to sci-hub for free basically it takes a few days to jailbreak them from the paywall just post in the arxiv under CS let me look into doing this. thanks for the tip pdf is here, please take further discussions to the thread below! highly recommend people check it out, good stuff this has aged a bit, the main thing being those PRs at the bottom, and the mechanics of the queue but otherwise a good high-level summary
